newsitem.title: UK: Salvesen marked up on dividend, demerger.
newsitem.headline: Salvesen marked up on dividend, demerger.

text.p: Shares in British transport and services firm Christian Salvesen were marked higher on Monday after the company unveiled a plan to spend 150 million pounds ($253 million) on special dividends and demerge its hire unit.

Salvesen shares, which hit a year's high of 366p in August on a takeover bid it rejected, were indicated at 330p in pre-market dealings, up six pence on the day. The broader market was indicated flat.
The dividend and demerger plans were announced with results for the half-year to September 30 which showed pretax profits up at 51.6 million pounds from 45 million a year earlier.
"The shares are up on the dividend and earnings which were pretty much in line so we're not sure we'll see any major gain today. It might draw attention to the stock though," one marketmaker said.
In addition to an ordinary dividend of 3.8p per share for the half year, Salvesen intends to pay an enhanced dividend of 17p now at a cost of about 50 million pounds.
"A foreign income dividend of approximately 100 million pounds will be paid before the end of March 1997," it said.
